decision.title: Streamed output and input in the JavaScript API (packet js-2)
decision.summary: The host shim and JavaScript API stream serialized output to a sink in chunks and read input from byte readers or chunk sources, so large outputs are not buffered whole.

body.p: , after , , , , , , , . The owner: "the JavaScript API will burn a lot of memory with large outputs because everything is buffered." Every serializing call wrote into the processor's output buffer, which the package then decoded into one string; the module's memory grows to fit the buffer and never shrinks.

item.p: Host shim (bindings/host/sxml_host.h, additive; not a public header, does not apply): an per processor, sxml_host_set_output(processor, {writer, chunk_byte_count}). With a writer, sxml_host_serialize, sxml_host_query_serialize and the serialized principal result of sxml_host_stylesheet_transform go to a chunk stream: the serializer's writes are gathered in a buffer of the chunk size (64 KiB by default, allocated for the call) and written as BYTES events when it is full and at the end; a write at least a chunk long that finds the buffer empty is written from where it is, a chunk at a time. Serialized result documents are written between RESULT_DOCUMENT_OPENED (its URI) and RESULT_DOCUMENT_CLOSED (is_abandoned) events, through a result document handler that delegates to the collector for RAW and TREE delivery; the buffer is flushed before each bound, so bytes before a bound belong to what was open before it, and dropped for an abandoned document. The output stream of the library (sxml_output_stream, serialize.h) already receives the bytes in pieces; nothing changes below the shim.

Byte readers ( through the shim): sxml_host_resource gains reader_identifier, and a resolver may answer SXML_RESOURCE_FORM_BYTE_READER; the processor's sxml_host_byte_reader (sxml_host_set_byte_reader: read into the buffer sxml lends, release when sxml stops reading) then serves it. sxml_host_transform_request gains streamed_source_uri (), after the side results, so existing word offsets stay. Swift's memberwise transform request gains the field (not compiled here: no Swift toolchain in this container); Kotlin's JNI uses designated initializers. Rejected: a writer or reader in the processor configuration (each host's constructor call would change), and a public incremental parse for Processor.parse ( rejected a reader in sxml_xml_parse_request; doc($uri) with a chunk source does it).

JavaScript (src/stream.ts, imports sxml_host.write, read, release_reader in sxml_javascript_stream.c): an (a function, or {write, close?, abort?}); Processor.serializeTo, Value.serializeTo, XQuery.serializeTo and runTo, PutDocument.serializeTo, TransformOptions.output, resultDocumentOutput(uri) (undefined gathers the document as text, as before) and streamedSource; ProcessorOptions.outputChunkByteCount. Each chunk is copied out of the module (the buffer is reused); an object sink is closed after the call, or aborted with the error when it fails, and a result document's sink when it is abandoned. A sink's exception stops the call and is rethrown, as the resolver's (); a sink or chunk source must not use its processor. A resolver may answer an XML document with a (an iterable of Uint8Array or string chunks, closed with return()); other kinds join the chunks. The string-returning methods are unchanged (additive API). Adapters: textSink (TextDecoder in stream mode, so characters split across chunks decode whole), writableStreamSink, nodeStreamSink, outputReadableStream.

Backpressure: an evaluation runs synchronously inside sxml.wasm, so a sink cannot make it wait. A sink that consumes each chunk at once (writeSync, a hash, a decoder feeding a parser, postMessage to a thread that reads concurrently) keeps memory bounded by one chunk; the stream adapters queue chunks in JavaScript memory until the call returns, which still spares the module's copy and the string. True backpressure would need the evaluation to suspend (JSPI or an asyncify build), not proposed.
Validation reports stay side results: they are objects, not serialized output.

Measured (Node.js 22, the wasm preset's module, output 108.7 MB of 1.8 million elements, written with fs.writeSync to /dev/null; module memory, peak JavaScript heap, peak resident set): value.serialize 749.2 MB, 112.6 MB, 859 MB; serializeTo 480.8 MB, 4.1 MB, 547 MB (the tree itself is the rest). query.run and runTo and transform from a template: the same. transform with xsl:source-document streamable="yes" (95.6 MB source): 791.2 MB, 1,048 MB resident; with a chunk source and a sink 481.4 MB, 570 MB (that shape builds the principal result). streamedSource with a streamable mode ('s streamed serialization): string source and string result 387.4 MB, 112.6 MB, 713 MB; chunk source and sink 10.6 MB, 14.6 MB, 172 MB.

Tests: tests/host_shim_test.c (chunks of 4 bytes, a failing write, back to the output; a document through the byte reader, released once, not available without a reader), 10 of 10 under ASan and UBSan. New javascript/streams (test/stream.test.ts, 19 cases): chunked output equals the strings for values, queries, fn:put and transformations, chunk sizes 1 to 4 split multi-byte characters and textSink joins them, result documents to sinks and gathered, aborts on a serialization error inside a result document, a throwing sink, a sink using its processor, the three adapters, chunk sources for fn:doc, unparsed-text, a throwing source and a streamed principal source, and a 100.4 MB output of a streamed source (a 2.6 MB chunk source) under 64 MB of module memory and 32 MB of JavaScript heap growth (about 4 s). javascript/package and javascript/languages pass unchanged. The book's JavaScript chapter: 6 examples match.
Sizes: sxml.wasm 13,450,808 bytes stripped / 2,377,893 gzipped (13,448,586 / 2,377,992 before this change, +2,222 bytes; budget 14,000,000 / 2,800,000, not raised).

Found: a streamed principal source whose stylesheet writes text with method text (an xsl:value-of per record) grows memory with the square of the output (20,000 records of 1 KB reach 4 GB, out of memory); with method xml and elements it stays at 11 MB. The text method's principal result is not a streamed serialization (), and adjacent text seems to be joined anew each time. Not fixed here (an evaluator matter); the default step limit also stops the streamed identity of 95 MB from the package, which has no option for it.
